cards.title: Scope and reading contract
items: Each numbered lane makes transformation inputs and outputs explicit. Repeated named tables/workbooks refer to the same data objects, not additional databases. Inter-lane references are textual; tracing follows the drawn arrows within each lane.

Lanes 13–14 expand selectable unresolved-only handoffs. Only Not Matched groups enter later stages. Matched and Review groups remain available for inspection and export. Review has no manual reclassification action.

The API also supports independent Email and Class runs from the original school file. It does not automatically remove students matched in another independent run. The chained route shown here uses only prior Not Matched outputs.
Invalid inputs fail the requested operation; they are not student Not Matched classifications. Session, transport, persistence, and security machinery are outside this diagram.

cards.title: Reference data and normalization
items: School reference: app/repositories/admission_dump_service.py selects users JOIN paid_users for user_edu_school and user_type=0, validates users_schools.school_id, and retains school identity.

SQL builds fullname and generated_col = lowercase full name without spaces + adjusted class. Package 14 uses class; package 12 uses class+1; package 11 uses class+2; otherwise class is unchanged. Uploaded references must already provide generated_col for Class mapping.

Reference fields include user_id, user_name, admission_number, user_firstname, user_lastname, fullname, user_email, user_edu_class, user_edu_major, user_package, generated_col. Nulls become empty strings and identical fetched rows are removed.
Parsing uses dtype=str and keep_default_na=False. Admission identifiers retain leading zeros: 00123 and 123 are different. Normalization is stage-specific, not a global fuzzy-matching pass.

cards.title: Admission rules in execution order
items: Missing admission → Not Matched. Repeated nonblank admission among deduplicated school rows → Review.
Missing school first name → Review, even if the admission has no reference hit. Multiple dump occurrences → Review with all source row numbers.
Otherwise no admission hit → Not Matched. One hit with missing dump first name, unequal first name, matching one-character name (after removing periods), or missing username → Review.
One admission hit with matching usable first names and username → provisional Matched. The endpoint passes name_is_full=False: the selected first-name cell is compared, not tokenized as a full name.

Duplicate nonblank usernames or user IDs among provisional Matched records → Review. Preserve audit evidence during overrides. Exact whole-row deduplication occurs before admission-number duplicate checks.

Append mapping_admission_number, mapping_username, mapping_user_id, mapping_first_name, mapping_dump_first_name, mapping_dump_row, mapping_dump_count, mapping_status. Export combines mapping_status with mapping_reason and removes the separate reason column.

cards.title: Email rules in execution order
items: Normalize selected emails with trim/lower. Empty values are excluded only from the query set; their school rows remain and become Not Matched.
Duplicate nonblank email in source rows → Review before dump candidate checks. Multiple dump records for an email → Review. Missing email or no candidates → Not Matched.

One candidate: compare trimmed lowercase first-name cells. Missing/different names or equal one-character names → Review. Equal usable names → provisional Matched. The optional sorted-full-name branch is not used by this endpoint.

For provisional Matched only: require selected school index and candidate user_edu_school, with equal normalized values. Missing/null/different school → Review. Then duplicate matched username or user ID → Review.
SQL looks across schools; school membership is checked after matching. Query normalization trims input emails, while SQL uses LOWER(user_email).

Exports remove Admission RESULT_COLUMNS, then append email_mapping_email, email_mapping_dump_full_name (the compared first name on this route), email_mapping_status, email_mapping_user_id, email_mapping_username. Internal _email_group is not exported.

cards.title: Full Name + Class rules
items: Input choice: school_file, admission_not_matched, or email_not_matched. Require nonempty source rows, selected name/class columns, and school reference generated_col.
Source key = trimmed lowercase full name with literal spaces removed + trimmed lowercase class value, with no separator. Reference keys are trimmed/lowercased generated_col values.
Missing full name or class → Not Matched. No candidate → Not Matched. Multiple candidates → Review. Exactly one candidate → provisional Matched.
Duplicate nonblank usernames or user IDs among provisional Matched records → Review. This classifier adds no first-name, school-membership, or required-username check.
Append full_name_class_generated_value, full_name_class_status, full_name_class_username, full_name_class_user_id. Preserve inherited source columns, including upstream audit columns if present.
Output names: full_name_class_matched.xlsx, full_name_class_review.xlsx, full_name_class_not_matched.xlsx. The last group is the final unresolved result.

cards.title: Review, generation, and downloads
items: Every mapping stores three independent XLSX workbooks with row counts, including header-only empty groups. Formula-like uploaded values remain literal text.

Review previews read saved workbooks. Admission preview may enrich candidate names and perform legacy display cleanup, without rerunning mapping or persisting reclassification. No group-transfer controls are available.

Combined workbook sheets: Admission Matched, Admission Review, Admission Not Matched, Email Matched, Email Review, Class Matched, Class Review, Final Not Matched. Only available saved groups are included.

Email Not Matched is individually downloadable but excluded from the combined workbook. Admission Not Matched remains included even after downstream runs. The final workbook does not reconcile repeated students across stages.
Replacing inputs or rerunning upstream stages can clear dependent saved results. Dropdown drafts alone do not commit a new mapping.

cards.title: Click details and synthetic examples
items: Click or keyboard-focus a node to open the native Semantic Passport. It displays the short description, compact field/value sample, and authored neighboring flows. This installed dataflow schema has no separate rich-object detail field; the complete examples are in these supporting cards.

All sample values below are synthetic documentation fixtures. No uploaded student files, database rows, credentials, or session files were read. Emails use the reserved example.invalid domain. Counts and exported rows were generated by the repository mapping functions.

Uploaded school headers are user-selected, not a fixed application schema. admission_number, first_name, email, name, and classNumber are representative headers already used in repository tests. Internal/output fields retain the exact names from the code.

Compact click samples show selected fields, not a whole row. Status and reason are combined in exported mapping_status, email_mapping_status, and full_name_class_status. Full structures below are text representations of workbook rows, not API JSON payloads.

cards.title: Normalized Student Records — admission-normalize
items: Admission comparison trims admission strings and lowercases/strips the selected first-name cell. It preserves original school columns. There is no standalone globally normalized student DTO.
Representative source row: {"admission_number": "00001", "first_name": "Alpha", "email": "alpha@example.invalid", "name": "Alpha Example", "classNumber": "3"}
Comparison values under the selected source headers: {"admission_number": "00001", "first_name": "alpha"}
Implementation: backend/app/services/admission_mapping/admission_row_classification.py and admission_name_comparison.py.

cards.title: Generated workbook data — download-input / final-write
items: build_workbook returns a dictionary with data (actual XLSX bytes) and count (row count). The data value below is only a textual placeholder, not the runtime value or a real file.
Representative wrapper: {"data": "<XLSX bytes omitted>", "count": 1}

Individual XLSX downloads return those bytes; CSV downloads parse the full workbook and encode UTF-8 with BOM. Final assembly reads available stage workbooks into separate sheets and returns XLSX bytes.
Implementation: backend/app/services/admission_mapping/admission_workbook.py; backend/app/services/final_results_workbook.py.
